answer: Each identity claims one distinct vine segment and locks a 70-credit bond. Its ember toll is 15 for the first identity on a segment, rising by 5 per identity already there, so the k-th pays 15+5(k-1). A falcon auditor recounts occupancy from the public vine ledger at epoch-end; over-cap sharing or a reused toll receipt burns the bond. A rented-segment ring fails: each ember receipt is key-signed per identity, so a mismatched key burns both bonds. 1,000 fakes piled on one segment cost 70,000 in bonds plus 2,512,500 in tolls; an honest identity pays 15 and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
